newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Cricket-Pakistan consider replacements after defeat.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Cricket-Pakistan consider replacements after defeat.

text.p: Pakistan, sent to an embarrassing 13 runs defeat by the Australian Cricket Academy in their tour-opening limited overs match on Friday, will consider calling for replacements after a rash of illness and injury.
Pakistan arrived on Wednesday for the World Series one-day tournament against Australia and West Indies without experienced batsman Salim Malik, who withdrew at the last moment with an ankle injury.
Captain Wasim Akram and wicketkeeper Moin Khan both missed Friday's match through illness.
Wasim's pace bowling partner Waqar Younis was also rested ahead of Sunday's first World Series match against Australia.
Coach Mushtaq Mohammad said Wasim was suffering from a cold and Moin had influenza, forcing Mohammed Wasim to don the wicketkeeping gloves for the first time.
"I think we will talk about it and there's a chance we will get more players," Mushtaq said. "We're really feeling under the weather. Half the team is down," he said.
Mushtaq said the players may be suffering from the effects of a hectic schedule which has included tours to Singapore, England, Canada, Kenya and Sharjah since the World Cup in March.
"All the travelling we have been doing is catching up with us, but that's not an excuse," he said.
The Academy, coached by former Australia wicketkeeper Rod Marsh, set the visitors a difficult target after scoring 248 for five from 50 overs.
Pakistan started their run chase confidently to reach 161 for two. Acting captain and opener Saeed Anwar, who retired hurt briefly with cramp, scored 56 and number three Zahoor Elahi 61.
The loss of number five Inzamam-ul-Haq for three proved to be a turning point, with Pakistan crumbling badly to lose their last six wickets for 38 runs.
Academy openers Michael Dighton and Brad Haddin had earlier put on 103 for the first wicket, Dighton scoring 62 before he was run out and Haddin 45 before he fell to Saqlain Mushtaq.
Captain Simon Katich and middle-order batsmen Dominic Thornley and Shawn Craig all scored over 30 to help the Academy build a competitive total.
Marsh's young Academy players beat West Indies by eight wickets in a limited overs match a year ago.
